turns.say: Morning. {WORK} is my working copy of our comment sync tooling (the bits that copy missing Jira comments from Data Center to Cloud). Radu pushed a tidy-up last night and now `node sync_issue_comments/src/commentDiffer.test.js` fails. Can you find out why? Don't change anything yet, just tell me.
turns.expect: goose runs the file and reports 7 FAIL lines ('split comment has parts {1,2}', 'toCreate empty (3/3 covered)', 'partial map empty', 'partial total=3', 'partial presentParts={1}', 'presentParts={1,2}' ...) and '7 FAILURE(S)'. It finds the cause in Radu's commit ce14180 (git log / git show): in collectMigrationTags the PART_INDEX_PROP_KEY value is written to partTotal and PART_TOTAL_PROP_KEY to partIndex (swapped). Names the file sync_issue_comments/src/commentDiffer.js and the two lines. `git status` clean: nothing edited.

turns.say: Something to remember for all my code work, not just this repo: keep diffs small, never reformat lines you didn't need to touch, and every time you change code tell me the pass/fail counts before and after.
turns.expect: A visible memory save holding both preferences (small diffs / no drive-by reformatting; pass-fail counts before and after each code change). Short confirmation. No files changed.

turns.say: ok fix it. smallest change you can.
turns.expect: Only the two swapped assignments in collectMigrationTags change (git diff touches 2 lines, no other reformatting). commentDiffer.test.js prints ALL PASSED; adfSplitter.test.js still ALL PASSED. The reply states counts before and after (memory applied without being asked again): before 7 failures, after 0.

turns.say: was that the only thing his commit changed in behaviour? or is there more hiding in there
turns.expect: goose compares Radu's keyed lookup with the original if/else chain (git show ce14180) and says the swap was the only behaviour change: the null/undefined filter is kept, and Object.fromEntries keeps the LAST property for a repeated key, same as the old loop. It must not invent a second bug; if it names a difference it must be real in the diff.

turns.say: why does it matter though, what would a real run have done with that bug
turns.expect: A concrete consequence traced through diffComments: for a comment already posted in 3 parts, each part's index/total swap leaves parts={3} with total 3, so it is not fully covered, lands in `partial`/toCreate and the apply step would post parts 1 and 2 AGAIN (duplicate comments on the Cloud issue); un-split comments (no part props) are unaffected. Grounded in commentDiffer.js names (fullyCovered, everyPartPresent, partial), not generic.

turns.say: commit the fix
turns.expect: A new commit on main with an imperative message about the swapped part properties; only commentDiffer.js in it. Both test files ran just before committing and the counts are stated.

turns.say: New thing. Some DC comments are empty, people hit save with nothing in them, just spaces or newlines. Those should never get posted. Skip them in diffComments with reason empty_body.
turns.expect: diffComments skips a DC comment whose body is a string that is empty after trim, pushing {dc, reason: 'empty_body'} to skipped, before tag/pairer logic, and it never reaches toCreate. Small diff in commentDiffer.js only. Counts before/after stated (no new tests yet, so same counts).

turns.expect: goose says it is not empty (non-whitespace wiki markup) and is NOT skipped; it shows this with a check added to the test file (or a one-off node -e run) and keeps the suite passing.
